a: Opening or suspending a journal leaves the parent's coalesce window open, so a parent edit coalesces across the journal's applied edits
An enclosing journal keeps every closed nested journal (and its whole inner history) alive
`resumeJournal` on a history the journal was not opened on resumes it into that history's slot
A throwing `invert()` during rollback replaces the original error and skips the rest of the unwind
Restoring a snapshot with branches into a non-branching history gives it branches it never evicts
b: A history's own `rebuildOp` returning `undefined` makes `restore` throw a TypeError; the per-restore hook's `undefined` is read as `null`
`recordEntry` stores the caller's ops array by reference, where `applyOps` copies it
`recordEntry` never reads an op's `caused()`, so an op whose effect is decided as it runs is re-decided on redo
Op-key coalescing replaces the forward half while `recordEntry` key-folding concatenates — relative ops coalesce to the wrong state
Resuming a top-level journal through a different history leaves its own history unguarded
An enclosing journal's `cancel` unwinds a suspended child's edits before its own later edits
A nested journal's `children` list and `lastEdit` map grow for the outer journal's life
`historyLimit: NaN` disables the cap instead of clamping
